name: United States federal law (CFR, U.S. Code, Federal Register, federal courts)
_doc: The base pack. Every other US pack is meant to be loaded ALONGSIDE this one, not instead of it, because almost every specialist citation eventually resolves to a title of the Code or the CFR.
_official_domains: Where these bodies of law officially live. `krokai review` merges these into its grounding so the lookalike detector knows the NAMES worth impersonating: measured in a sister project, `uscis.com` - the exact agency name in a foreign zone - walked past a detector that only knew the `gov`/`mil` labels. Registrable domains only, no subdomains: the first label is what the detector learns, and deriving `travel` from `travel.state.gov` would put a warning on `travel.com`.

shapes._what: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(6)(i)(D) — title + part is the address; the subsection tail rides along for display but is not part of the key, because a file holding part 214 holds every subsection of it.

address.label: %s CFR part %s
address._reject_doc: R77 (#333 class): part numbers repeat across TITLES — 26 CFR also has a part 245 — and the part-only and body rules cannot see the title. The negative guard rejects a file whose own head explicitly names a DIFFERENT title; a head naming no title stays soft, which keeps eCFR downloads whose head says only 'Title 8' matchable via the second scan.

file_match._what: Three or more section numbers of the form 214.x is what a real part looks like; one stray mention is a cross-reference in someone else's document.

shapes._what: 8 U.S.C. § 1255(k). Accepts U.S.C., USC, U. S. C.

address.label: %s U.S.C. § %s
address._reject_doc: R77 (#333, lunapro): the filename rule asked for 'usc' and the section but never the TITLE, so 26USC-1255 satisfied a key for 8 U.S.C. § 1255 — a different statute under the same section number. The CFR rule one shape up always carried its title; this one had lost it. A title-bearing filename form is preferred, the title-less form stays for real download names (USCODE-2024-title8-section1255) but under the same negative guard as the CFR shape: a head that explicitly names a different title rejects the file.

file_match._what: Two bare occurrences AND at least one that is explicitly a section reference. Either test alone is noise: a four-digit number occurs everywhere, and a single section sign proves nothing about which section the file is.
GPO text carries [[Page NNNNN]] markers, which is how a pincite into a Federal Register preamble is recovered at all.

shapes._what: Party names. This is the address of a case; the reporter cite below is its shelf mark.
shapes.sample: in Kazarian v. USCIS the court held

shapes._what: Reporter citations. Recognised so they show up next to a quotation as its neighbours, but NOT used as an address: a volume-and-page pair alone cannot tell you which downloaded PDF it is.

Bare section references — «Section 245.2(a)», «§ 1255(k)», «§§ 1182». Ported from the sister project in R76 (#323), where 103 such references were invisible: the near/far rings stayed empty and a NOT_FOUND beside one was misclassified «evidentiary». Recognised as a NEIGHBOUR only, like the reporter shape above — a bare section number cannot name its title, so it is not an address. The digit must follow the marker immediately (the sister project's guard), and `(?<!\.\s)` keeps this from double-matching the tail of «U.S.C. §»/«C.F.R. §»/«Reg. §» forms, whose own shapes already fire.
shapes.sample: relief is unavailable under Section 245.2(a) here
